restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages with equal digests for the Orchard hash with 9 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r9-prefix-v1), found as a collision F(x) = F(y), x != y, of the walk F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE: message() is the injective parametrisation of the input line on which rounds 0 and 1 are affine, OUTSCALE a fixed nonzero field constant, rho0 a random 254-bit coin of the attempt. Plain birthday search, one trail with distinguished points, one table; the success probability uses no property of the rounds.

Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 405. Prices used: canonical field ADD and MUL 1/C each; every other primitive 256-bit word operation (AND, OR, shift, compare, branch, register move, aligned load or store, random word) 1/C. No permutation call is charged as a unit: every evaluation executes the 248-operation step program (97 ADD, 151 MUL; proof.md Section 2, listing in Appendix C), an equivalent form of rounds 2-63 that equals the reference digest divided by OUTSCALE. Constant loads: the 94 step constants are loaded once per attempt (94 loads, charged) into a declared file of 155 256-bit registers, counted in memory; arithmetic takes register operands.

Ledger (proof.md Section 6, instruction listings): a trail step is 248 + 3 operations, plus 3 per block of 4 unrolled steps; a recovery evaluation at most 248 + 6; table scan, insertion, bisection, constant loads, the message roots and setup are at most 15,442,595,772 operations. The offline derivation of the step constants and fixed parameters (build_step, tune, plan) is bounded by 401,576,999,984 word operations from stated caps (proof.md Section 6a); that bound is inside time_log2 and is also declared as preprocessing_log2 = 30 (one quantity, not added twice). time_log2 is the full budget with every halt charged at its limit: S = n + d trail steps and 3 gmax recovery evaluations, log2 T = 126.795512, claimed 126.79552 (rounded up). One attempt; no restart, amplification or advice.

Memory: 28,509 table entries of one 32-byte word (high 126 bits of the value OR index), a side array of 16-bit low parts (1,782 words), the start word, code at most 1,969 instructions at 36 bytes, constants and the 155-register file: 1,048,548 bytes, below 2^20 (proof.md Section 7; the code term and the word layout are derived there).

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 (proof.md Section 5) proves 0.620000002788068819 (at least 0.62) for a uniformly random function at the filed budget, and 0.39 at a budget 1.3992 times smaller (0.4846 bit of the claimed time), with explicit terms for the trail, detection, table and gaps. H1 (the only premise, score-critical, an assumption, no proof is known) states that the real map with the random coin rho0 reaches 0.39 at the filed budget; measurements of the real map family at r = 7, 23 and 56 on truncated outputs are in proof.md Section 8.

The program is printed in full in proof.md Appendix B (standard library only); the step program in Appendix C. One organizer-run experiment is declared (lowbits-birthday, python-message-pairs-v1, event digest-xor-mask; source experiments/exp_lowbits.py): agreement of the first 14 bits of this target's own digest, a reduced event that witnesses nothing about full width, cost or the success probability (proof.md Section 9). Participant measurements: replay sources in Appendix D, data in Appendix E, per-job seeds and records in Appendix F. No full collision is produced or claimed; the claim is the cost of the search.

heuristics.statement: Let n0 = 133586789 * 2^100 be the number of trail steps at which the Lemma 2 bound for a uniformly random function is 0.39. The filed trail has n = 186920058 * 2^100 = 1.3992 n0 steps (0.4846 bit more time), at which Lemma 2 gives 0.620000002 for a uniformly random function. Premise: for the attempt's coins rho0 and x_0 (uniform 254-bit words), the search of proof.md Section 3 on the real map F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE, at the budget n, succeeds with probability at least 0.39. This is an assumption; no proof is known.
heuristics.scope: Target poseidon-orchard-r9-prefix-v1, inputs on the line of proof.md Section 1, one trail with the parameters of proof.md Section 3 (S = 2.370e38 evaluations). Not claimed for other round counts or budgets. Only the success probability rests on it; the step program, the recovery, the ledger and the memory are proved or checked exactly (proof.md Sections 2, 4, 6, 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-run experiment lowbits-birthday (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask, 256 trials; proof.md Section 9): regime = this target's own digest at r = 9, agreement of the first 14 bits, fresh random inputs, at most 1200 evaluations per trial (a random function needs about 160); it witnesses that the real digest has no gross low-bit structure at one reduced width, and the runner infers no probability. Sensitivity of that experiment: if the 14-bit collision rate were c times the random one, a trial needs more than 1200 evaluations with probability exp(-43.95 c), so 256 of 256 successes is expected with probability 0.99 or more only for c >= 0.23; it cannot separate c = 0.5 from c = 1, so the margin down to c = 0.511 rests on the participant measurements. Participant measurements (not organizer-run; per-job seeds, records and counts in proof.md Appendix F) on the real map family at r = 7, 23 and 56 partial rounds with outputs truncated to w = 16..40 bits (F_w(v) = low w bits of F(v), a fresh rho and start per trial, as in the attempt), 20,616 walks: the hazard multiplier (collision rate relative to a random function, estimated from the exact discrete first-repeat law, profile-likelihood interval, coverage checked by simulation in proof.md Section 8) is 1.001, 95% interval [0.987, 1.015], with slope -0.0011 per bit (standard error 0.0015) across widths; the full search succeeded in 3,463/8,616 = 0.402 runs at widths 24..40 against a mean Lemma 2 bound of 0.3900; DP gaps follow the geometric law and stayed below gmax. Extrapolation from these widths to 254 bits and 2^127 steps, and to r = 9, is by this premise. Sensitivity: if the real map has the collision rate of a random function times a factor c, success is about 1 - exp(-c x) - n/N - eps with x = 0.96976; it stays at least 0.39 for every c >= 0.511 (a deficit of up to 48.9 percent); c = 1, 0.9, 0.75, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4 give the values in the table of proof.md Section 8.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer experiment is one width (14 bits), one round count and a witness-only event on the digest, not on the walk map F. The participant measurements reach outputs of at most 40 bits and trails of at most 2,970,429 steps, at three round counts; they show the random-function collision law of the real round function at these widths and do not bound the collision rate at 254 bits. On a single fixed map the success over starts varies with that map's longest cycle; the attempt therefore draws rho0, and H1 concerns the average over rho0.
